extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and USPTO examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for determining, asserting, maintaining, and losing U.S. USPTO small entity status (eligibility for reduced patent fees), including who may sign/assert, what transfers/licenses affect status, timing and form of assertions, certification consequences, and government-license exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: All U.S. rights must be owned by small entities to claim reduced fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment of reduced fees under 35 U.S.C. 41 is limited to situations in which all of the rights in the invention are owned by small entities (persons, small business concerns, or nonprofit organizations). Transfer of rights to a non-small entity will disqualify an applicant from claiming small entity status; if rights transferred to a non-small entity are later returned to a small entity so that all rights are held by small entities, reduced fees may be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and examples: rights in question are those in the United States to be covered by an application or patent (transfer of rights to a foreign patent alone does not affect US small entity status). The Office will generally not question assertions made in accordance with the section, but fraud provisions apply (see fraud entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of licenses and types that disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: The term “license” includes nonexclusive as well as exclusive licenses and royalty-free as well as royalty-generating licenses. A grant of a non-exclusive license to a non-small entity will disqualify an applicant from claiming small entity status. Implied licenses to use and resell patented articles purchased from a small entity will not preclude claiming small entity status. An order to a firm to build a prototype for the applicant’s own use is not considered a license for purposes of the definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ulead Systems, Inc. v. Lex Computer & Management Corp., 351 F.3d 1139 (Fed. Cir. 2003) cited for a non-exclusive license to a non-small entity disqualifying status. Be careful: presence of implied licenses from sale typically does not disqualify; explicit nonexclusive licenses to non-small entities do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security interests do not transfer rights unless default occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: A security interest does not involve an obligation to transfer rights in the invention under 37 CFR 1.27(a)(1)-(a)(3) unless the security interest is defaulted upon. Only if the loan is defaulted upon will the security interest permit a transfer of rights in the application or patent to the secured party, which may cause loss of small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: granting a security interest to a bank (a large entity) does not presently prohibit claiming small entity status; upon default, status may be lost. If loss occurs due to default, notification obligations apply (see notification entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion of entitlement is required to establish small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish small entity status for paying small entity fees, a party must make an assertion of entitlement to small entity status in the application or patent in the manner set forth in 37 CFR 1.27(c)(1) (written assertion) or 1.27(c)(3) (payment of certain exact small entity fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written assertion must be clearly identifiable, signed, and convey the concept of entitlement (no required specific wording). The assertion can be a simple sentence or a checked box on a transmittal letter; written assertions will be liberally interpreted. Payment of the exact amount of certain small entity basic filing, transmittal, international search, or basic national fees will be treated as a written assertion (see the separate entry on assertion-by-payment). Payment of other small entity fees (or wrong amounts) will not be treated as an assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by payment of exact small-entity basic filing/national/international fees treated as written assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment, by any party, of the exact amount of one of the small entity basic filing fees (see §§ 1.16(a)-(e)), the small entity transmittal fee (§ 1.445(a)(1) or § 1.1031(a)), the small entity international search fee (§ 1.445(a)(2) to a Receiving Office other than USRO), or the small entity basic national fee (§ 1.492(a)) will be treated as a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status, even if the type of basic filing/fee is inadvertently selected in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office accords small entity status based on payment of an inapplicable small entity basic filing or national fee, any balance due will be charged with appropriate surcharge (§ 1.16(f) or (g)). Payment of other small entity fees (or incorrect amounts) is not sufficient to establish status. The small entity first part of individual designation fee to the IB (§ 1.1031) is also treated as an assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign a written assertion (applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the written assertion of entitlement to small entity status may be signed by: (1) the applicant (per 37 CFR 1.42 or 1.421); (2) a patent practitioner of record or practitioner acting in representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34; (3) the inventor or joint inventor if the inventor is the applicant; or (4) the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change aligns with practice on who is the applicant. The assignee can sign even if not the applicant or a juristic entity; joint inventors who are applicants may have one inventor sign to establish status for the application. See MPEP § 509.03(a) for interactions with multiple inventors/assignees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign/file a written assertion (applications filed before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012 (pre-AIA), the written assertion can be signed by parties identified in § 1.33(b) (e.g., registered attorney/agent), by at least one individual identified as an inventor (even if pre-AIA 1.63 oath/declaration not submitted), or by an assignee of an undivided part interest (though partial assignee cannot file without a party identified under § 1.33(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA distinctions: an actual inventor who has not been identified as an inventor in the file may not file a written assertion; where a later-filed oath/declaration changes the listed inventors, an original written assertion previously submitted remains unless changed by an appropriate party under § 1.27(g)(2). Partial assignees may sign but not necessarily file without recourse to appropriate parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion must be made in each related/continuing/reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Status as a small entity must be specifically established by an assertion in each related, continuing, and reissue application in which status is appropriate and desired. Status in one application or patent does not affect the status of any other application or patent, regardless of relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refiling under § 1.53 as continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part, or filing a reissue requires a new assertion. Filing an RCE (§ 1.114) does not require a new determination or assertion since it is not a new application. Provisional applications may establish small entity status by complying with 37 CFR 1.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: when small entity fees can be paid and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fee (other than the small entity basic filing fees and small entity national fees referenced in 1.27(c)(3)) can be paid in the small entity amount only if it is submitted with, or subsequent to, the submission of a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status (except refunds permitted by § 1.28(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: submit a written assertion before paying most small-entity-level fees. The payments listed in 1.27(c)(3) are treated as assertions themselves (see earlier entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one assertion required per application while status remains
rubrics_metrics.description: An assertion of small entity status need only be filed once in an application or patent. Small entity status, once established, remains in effect until changed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.27(g)(1). Where an assignment of rights to other small entities occurs after an assertion, a second assertion is not required. If small entity status is withdrawn under paragraph (g)(2), a new written assertion is required to obtain small entity status again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status remains for the prosecution of that application/patent until changed as specified; keep records of assertions. Withdrawal requires new written assertion to reinstate.

rubrics_metrics.name: New determination and notification required at issue and maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Once small entity status has been established in an application or patent, small entity fees may be paid thereafter without regard to a change in status until the issue fee is due or any maintenance fee is due. A new determination of entitlement is needed when issue or maintenance fees are due. Notification of loss of entitlement must be filed in the application or patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest of the issue fee or any maintenance fee due after the date on which small entity status is no longer appropriate. The notification must be a specific written assertion signed by a party identified in § 1.33(b); payment of a non-small entity fee alone is not sufficient notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when paying the issue fee in an application previously accorded small entity status and the new determination reveals loss of status, applicant should (A) check the appropriate box on Part B of the PTOL-85 to indicate change in entity status and (B) pay the non-small entity fee amount—do not just cross out prior recitation or merely pay the larger fee without written notification. See MPEP § 509.03(b) and § 509.03(g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and penalties for improperly claiming small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt to fraudulently establish status as a small entity, or pay fees as a small entity, shall be considered a fraud practiced or attempted on the Office. Improperly and with intent to deceive establishing status or paying small entity fees shall be considered fraud on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: fraud on the Office may lead to penalties and affect the application/patent. Applicants should make a determination of entitlement prior to asserting status (37 CFR 1.27(f)) and be aware that assertions carry certifications (see certification entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion and payment constitute certifications under 37 CFR 11.18 and signature rules under 37 CFR 1.4
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(4), an assertion of entitlement to small entity status (including payment of an exact small entity basic filing fee) inherently contains a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b). The person inserting a signature certifies the signature is his/her own and must have a reasonable basis to believe authenticity; violations may lead to sanctions under § 11.18(c)-(d). 37 CFR 11.18(b) requires that by presenting any paper the party certifies: statements of own knowledge are true; legal contentions are warranted or nonfrivolous; allegations have evidentiary support or likely will after investigation; denials of factual contentions are warranted or based on lack of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: asserting small entity status carries legal attestation—applicants/practitioners should ensure factual/legal bases and retain evidence of signature authenticity. False or frivolous assertions risk sanctions and criminal penalties (18 U.S.C. 1001) per § 11.18(b) and accompanying discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government licenses, CRADA, and Federal agency exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to a Federal agency resulting from a funding agreement under 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(4) will not preclude claiming small entity status provided: (A) the subject invention was made solely by employees of the small business concern or nonprofit organization; or (B) in the case of a Federal employee co-inventor, the Federal agency took action under 35 U.S.C. 202(e)(1) to exclusively license or assign whatever rights it currently holds or may acquire to the small business/nonprofit, subject to the license under 202(c)(4). For CRADA-related government use licenses under 15 U.S.C. 3710a(b), claiming small entity status is not prohibited in certain circumstances (e.g., retaining title to invention made solely by the small business/nonprofit, or government laboratory waived ownership or exclusively licensed ownership rights to the small entity). Additionally, specific situations described in 37 CFR 1.27(a)(4)(i) (e.g., use license to Government under rights determination Executive Order 10096, action under 15 U.S.C. 3710d(a), or retention under 35 U.S.C. 202(d) with conditions) do not constitute a license that prohibits small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government organizations themselves cannot qualify as nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) limitation). Universities and institutions of higher education qualify even with some government affiliation. Wholly owned subsidiaries of a nonprofit/university are considered part of the nonprofit/university for small entity qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners’ suggested form paragraph and practical filing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may use a form paragraph to notify applicants they may qualify for small entity status: the application may qualify for 'Small Entity Status' and applicant must make determination under 37 CFR 1.27(f) and an assertion under 1.27(c) before fees can be paid in the small entity amount; assertion must be signed, clearly identifiable, and convey entitlement; no particular form required. If applicant qualifies as small entity they may also qualify for micro entity under 37 CFR 1.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: written assertions are liberally interpreted; a simple sentence or checked box suffices. Remind applicants about micro entity possibility and to ensure assertions comply with signature and certification rules.
